name: FrugalGPT: How to Use Large Language Models While Reducing Cost and Improving Performance
problem: API pricing across strong models differs by orders of magnitude, so naively calling an expensive model for every query is economically indefensible at scale.
mechanism: A cost-and-accuracy study rather than a system: it measures cost and quality across a ladder of models and then shows three strategy families — LLM cascade (fall back to a cheaper model when the strong one is unsure), LLM router (pick the model up front) and LLM approximation (reuse a cached/smaller answer) — each with its own Pareto curve.
speedup_reported: Per the paper's framing: up to two orders of magnitude cost reduction while matching or improving accuracy over the strongest single model, across published workloads. These are API-PRICE savings against a baseline of always calling the most expensive model — not throughput, latency or GPU utilisation gains. The paper is a study of three strategy families (cascade, router, approximation), each with its own Pareto curve, so a single '2x' is only meaningful once the strategy and budget are named.
